info.name: ICP Calls — Phase A (manual test kit)
info.description:
Ready-made requests for the Phase A calls API.

Setup:
1. `npm run migrate --prefix backend`
2. `npm run seed:calls --prefix backend` (prints the demo password once)
3. Import this collection and calls.postman_environment.json, select the environment.
4. Put the printed password into the five *Password variables.
5. Run the folders in order (Collection Runner runs them in order too).

Every request asserts its expected result; a green run means the policy held.
Invites are rate limited per user (default 10 per minute). If you see 429
CALL_RATE_LIMITED, wait a minute or raise CALL_INVITE_RATE_MAX in backend/.env.
Access tokens are short-lived; re-run the login folder if you get 401.

item.name: 1) Policy matrix — denials
item.description: Ordinary employees may never call the Director or Deputy. Denials must look identical for existing, unknown and inactive targets, and for a self-call.

request.description: Every target-side denial must be indistinguishable from the others: same status, code and message.

item.name: Employee 1 → unknown employee id (expect the same 403 body)

request.description: This is the oracle test: an unknown target must be indistinguishable from the Director.

exec: pm.test('same code as the Director denial', () => pm.expect(body.code).to.eql('CALL_TARGET_FORBIDDEN'));
pm.test('same message as the Director denial', () => pm.expect(body.error).to.eql(pm.environment.get('deniedMessage')));

item.name: 2) Policy matrix — allowed
item.description: Leadership may call anyone, including each other. Ordinary employees may call each other across units.

item.name: 3) Lifecycle — invite → accept → end
item.description: Employee 1 (section u53) calls Employee 2 (directorate u24). Different units, no relationship required.

item.name: Employee 2 unread count unchanged (decline created nothing)

item.name: 7) Leadership redaction & missed_call
item.description: The Director calls Employee 1. Employee 1 must see فقط the configured label, cannot call back, and gets relay-only ICE. Marking it missed creates the only call notification.

item.name: Employee 1 history shows the same redacted entry
Employee 1 marks the call as missed
Employee 1 notifications use the redacted label

exec: pm.test('missed_call notification uses the label', () => pm.expect(list.some((n) => n.summary === expected)).to.eql(true));
pm.test('notification does not leak the Director name', () => pm.expect(list.some((n) => (n.summary || '').indexOf('مدير المصلحة (تجريبي)') !== -1)).to.eql(false));

item.name: 8) Settings — read, edit, verify live, restore
item.description: Any authenticated user can read /api/settings/app; only an admin can change it. The label is read at view time, so an edit applies to the next view and to new notifications without a restart.

item.name: PATCH app settings as ordinary employee (expect 403)
PATCH app settings as admin (edit the Director label)
GET settings shows the edited label
Employee 1 sees the edited label (no restart)
PATCH app settings as admin (restore the default)
Employee 1 sees the restored label on the next view

exec: pm.test('restored label applied to the existing call', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().call.caller.name).to.eql(pm.environment.get('directorRedactedLabel')));

item.name: 9) Admin oversight (metadata only)
item.description: Only admin/auditor may read GET /api/calls/oversight. It returns calls that involved the Director or Deputy as metadata only: no names, avatars, employee ids, SDP or ICE. Ordinary employees get 403.

exec: pm.test('no participant identity is returned', () => pm.expect(calls.every((c) => !('caller' in c) && !('callee' in c) && !('callerEmployeeId' in c) && !('calleeEmployeeId' in c))).to.eql(true));
pm.test('metadata is present', () => pm.expect(calls.every((c) => c.metadata && typeof c.metadata === 'object')).to.eql(true));
